blocks.x: Providers run 24/7 operations on clinical goodwill: clinician burden, throughput, revenue-cycle leakage and patient experience all compete for the same attention. Systems that industrialize documentation, coding and workflow intelligence give clinicians their time back — the only resource that matters.

The workflows we industrialize here: Clinical documentation, Prior authorization, Coding and CDI, Patient throughput, Clinical asset management. Each arrives with its current cycle times measured in the Diagnose phase, and each leaves the program governed by outcome SLOs rather than anecdotes.

items: Notes, orders and inbox consume evening hours; ambient tools stall on EHR integration and compliance sign-off.
Authorization, coding and denials consume revenue-cycle staff; denials cite missing documentation that existed.
Legacy devices, flat networks and vendor access make hospital ransomware credible; clinical continuity planning thin.
Outcome and throughput analytics depend on extracts; cohorts take days to define.
Mobile equipment (pumps, monitors) untracked; utilization and maintenance run on scavenger hunts.
DICOM archives grow unmanaged; storage spend rises while retrieval slows.

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: visit audio to structured notes in EHR with sign-off — documentation time down 25%+
criteria mapped to chart evidence; submissions assembled — turnaround down 60%
segmentation, recovery drills and manual fallbacks — restart time proven
FHIR-native cohorts with terminology services — cohort queries in minutes
pump/monitor tracking with maintenance prediction — utilization up 15-25%

blocks.x: A typical program here starts with a two-week diagnostic that measures the workflows named above and locks the baseline, moves through a gated proof on your data, then industrializes on platform rails with the sector's compliance evidence generated in-flight.

items: Clinicians get 90 minutes a day back — ambient documentation inside the EHR
Prior authorization turnaround down 62% — clinical evidence assembled automatically
